text:
alex kim: Quick heads-up — weekly capacity audit. I pulled the per-region GPU-hour runway and there's a weird drop in SFO-2 cluster usable hours for next week (nodes showing degraded NICs).
maya singh: saw that on the dashboard earlier. Is it the new 8-node subnet we rolled last month?
devon lee: yes, SFO-2 staging->prod subnet had a firmware update last night. A couple of cards (gpu-3,gpu-7) reported packet drops and PM reset loops. Kernel logs attached below.
ops-bot: [alert] 2012345600 - NIC flaps detected on sfo2-pool-4 (gpu-3, gpu-7). Auto-drain initiated.
sophia rivera: if they're drained, that reduces our effective throughput by ~13% for SFO-2 during peak hours. Can we absorb in SFO-1 or us-west-az?
raj patel: cost-wise, moving load to SFO-1 is fine short-term, but cross-region egress will increase token costs for a handful of enterprise customers bound to SFO region. Finance flagged any >10% cross-region shift last quarter.
finance-bot: FYI: estimated incremental network egress cost for 72h cross-region failover = $1.4k.
alex kim: okay — action plan: 1) devon triages NIC firmware+kernel signature, 2) maya prepares a canary overflow to sfo-1 with routing policy TTL=30s, 3) sophia to update capacity forecast spreadsheet.
devon lee: triage update: reproduced reset loop locally in staging. Suspect driver mismatch after vendor patch. Reverting to prior driver version stabilizes. Will request a controlled rollback on sfo2-pool-4.
maya singh: routing changes ready. Canary config (small portion of GA traffic):
```yaml
route_policy:
  - region_preference: sfo-2
  - fallback: sfo-1
  - canary_pct: 5
  - connection_ttl_s: 30
```
maya singh: planning to flip at 09:15 PT tomorrow during low peak; will monitor latency and token-per-req throughput.
sophia rivera: updated runway numbers in sheet: total GPU-hours by region for next 7 days updated. Key deltas: SFO-2 -13% (drain), SFO-1 +5% (canary), US-EAST unchanged, EU-WEST +2% reserved for enterprise rollouts.
alex kim: important: we need a short-term provisioning plan if rollback doesn't clear all bad cards. Options: hot-add spot GPUs in us-west-az (cheap but preemptible) or spin up 4 reserved in SFO-1 (more costly). What's our preferred?
raj patel: finance preference = mix: try spot hot-adds for non-SLA traffic, reserve 2 dedicated nodes in SFO-1 for SLA customers. Net incremental cost estimate (48h) = $2.2k hybrid vs $3.7k full-reserve.
ops-bot: [deploy] routing canary prepared, pending manual approval.
alex kim: I'll approve the canary at 09:15 PT tomorrow. devon, aim to have rollback approved by infra change window 08:30 so we avoid overlap.
devon lee: noted. I'll file the change request now and ping infra-oncall.
sophia rivera: FYI on forecasting: if rollback works, SFO-2 runway recovers to +4% by Wednesday. If rollback fails and we need full reserve, we'll hit our weekly spare buffer and need to tap the burst quota (request to cloud ops).
maya singh: adding a small alert tweak — raise token latency threshold for canary to 450ms for first 15 minutes so we don't get noisy pages.
alex kim: perfect. I'll summarize in the incident tracker and mark this thread as the coordination source. Action items: devon (rollback + CR), maya (canary + routing), sophia (forecast update + burst request if needed), raj (confirm finance approval for hybrid spend).
ops-bot: [note] follow-up: please post postmortem if rollback leads to customer impact.
raj patel: finance approves up to $3k emergency spend for this window. Keep receipts.
alex kim: thanks all. I'll update #eng-infra pins with the forecast snapshot and the canary link after 09:15.
